next_step: Finalize SOW for reserved GPU pools; procurement exec call week of 2026-03-15
notes: Elevator: Aegis Horizon runs a global concierge + itinerary generation platform (travel booking marketplace). Wants reserved GPU pools for low-latency chat + reranking during peak search windows.

Primary ask: Dedicated capacity Sizing + SLA language that supports p95 latency targets for live agent chat and deterministic throughput guarantees during peak events (e.g. Black Friday travel peaks).
Latency/throughput targets: p95 end-to-end chat latency <= 180ms (token-level streaming allowed), baseline concurrent sessions 250, burst to 800 concurrent sessions for 10-20 minute peaks.
Token profile: average 28 tokens/sec per active session during typing bursts; typical request < 60 tokens. Expected sustained token rate during peak: ~22400 tokens/sec.
Model preferences: primary inference on quantized Llama-3-70B q4x for quality; fallback to Llama-3-13B quantized for autoscale/failover. POC will measure quality delta vs latency.

Reserved GPU planning (initial proposal): Primary region NA-East: 12 x A100-equivalent GPUs (baseline); NA-West: 6 x GPUs (regional load + burst); EU-West: 6 x GPUs (replicated capacity for EU customers & failover).

Failover/headroom policy: maintain 30% cross-region failover headroom (warm-standby pool). In practice reserve +20% warm pool in primary and +10% cross-region reserve for failover. Aim for RTO < 90s for regional failover with active prefix/KV cache warmup strategy.

Throughput guarantees: Redwood to guarantee minimum sustained throughput per region (example SLA line): NA-East >= 160 concurrent sessions equivalent @ p95 <= 180ms, NA combined >= 250 concurrent sessions. Credits if sustained drop below 99.95% of reserved throughput windowed over 1 hour.

Autoscaling/bursting: requirement for burst topping to cloud spare capacity up to +40% for 15m windows without violating latencies; prefer predictable preemptible/burst capacity priced separately in SOW.

Caching & batching notes: Must support prefix KV caching across pool; request Redwood to size KV cache on GPU memory map with recommended cache TTL and eviction thresholds — client supplied sample trace in drive sizing workbook.

Networking & residency: VPC peering + private egress; egress cost sensitivity flagged by finance (target < $0.02/token-equivalent). Customer requires EU data residency for EU users, plus audit logs for all inference calls stored 90 days.

Security asks: SSO (SAML) integration completed in sandbox; needs KMS/HSM compatibility for model key wrapping, SOC2 attestation and audit_logging for all token-level events. Expect security questionnaire in drive completed 2026-01-10.

POC milestones (past + upcoming): 2026-01-05 discovery call (Lena/Diego); 2026-01-12 security QA submitted; 2026-02-01 sizing workbook shared; 2026-02-20 POC alpha (NA-East small reserved pool, synthetic load); 2026-03-01 POC results review (latency & quality metrics).

POC result summary: alpha hit p95=165ms with 12 GPUs baseline for NA-East using batching policy X. Observed KV cache hit of 42% reduced token work by ~27%. Need to test cross-region failover and warm-cache behavior.

Negotiation points: require 99.95% uptime for dedicated pool, explicit maintenance windows (2x/month with 48h notice), SLA credits calc example, and a 6-month trial pricing band for first-year reserved commitment.

Routing & rollouts: want traffic steering by region with policy to failover to smaller model variant (13B) if reserved capacity saturates. Also want canary rollouts for model version updates with automatic fallback to previous pinned version.

Cost sensitivity: procurement target is to keep estimated token-unit cost within 20% of current self-hosted run-rate. Redwood Optimize recommendations for quantization + batching will be evaluated to hit target ARR band.
Quote from CTO (paraphrased): 'We need predictable latency under heavy competition windows — if you can guarantee throughput and a clear failover plan, we'll move committed capacity.'
Risk items: cross-region cache warmup time, DKIM/MTU issues on VPC peering in NA-West, egress unpredictability for EU traffic during failover. Proposed mitigations in sizing workbook.

Next steps (detailed): 1) Finalize SOW with explicit GPU counts per region + headroom calc (Redwood to provide cost delta for +10% and +30% headroom); 2) Exec-level procurement call wk of 2026-03-15; 3) Legal to sign MSA with SLA addendum; 4) POC beta to validate cross-region RTO and model fallback by 2026-03-31.
